verbs.name: edit.color_space
verbs.description: Tag a media clip's INPUT color space — the space its SOURCE footage is in (a log / sRGB / Rec.2020 source). The renderer then converts the clip INTO the project working space (project.color), and on to the output space, before grade/effects — so a wide-gamut or screen-capture clip is correctly interpreted instead of being treated as Rec.709. Supported: rec709 (the assumed default for untagged clips), rec2020, srgb, linear; an unknown name is rejected with the supported list. Omitting `input` (or null) CLEARS the tag — the source is then assumed to already be in the working space, and the clip renders byte-identical to an untagged clip. A per-clip attribute (like edit.grade): video media clips only (audio/captions have no pixels), replay-safe, no filesystem/network touch. Conversion is ffmpeg `zscale` (input→working→output); a tagged clip forces the SOFTWARE render path.

clip.description: Clip id (a media clip on a video track)

input.description: Source color space of this clip's footage; omit/null to clear the tag

include_inverse.description: Deprecated compatibility option. Accepted for v0.6 callers but new operations use recompute-by-replay and have no inverse payload to include.

verbs.result: {op} — committed-op ride-along; the before/after input space is in op.effects[].detail

verbs.name: edit.color_match
verbs.description: Match a media clip's COLOUR/tonality to a REFERENCE clip — the colorist "make this shot match that shot" tool. Samples ONE representative mid-clip frame from each of clip (target) and reference, computes per-channel mean+std (RGB Reinhard-style transfer), and DERIVES an edit.grade correction: brightness from the luma-mean delta, contrast from the luma-std ratio, saturation from the chroma ratio, temperature_k from the warm/cool (R-B) mean delta — scaled by strength (0 = identity/no-op, 1.0 = full match, default 1.0). The correction is APPLIED through the normal edit.grade path, so it composes / undoes / replays like any per-clip grade (it OVERWRITES any existing grade on the clip). The colour ANALYSIS is live (it decodes frames once); the COMMITTED op is a plain, replay-safe grade (concrete params, no resampling on replay). Matching a clip to itself derives an identity grade (clears the grade). v1 LIMITATIONS: single mid-clip frame per side; plain RGB (LAB is the perceptual fast-follow); edit.grade has no green-magenta tint knob, so only the warm/cool axis is corrected. Video media clips only.

clip.description: Target clip id (a media clip on a video track) — the shot to correct

reference.description: Reference clip id (a media clip) — the look to match toward

strength.description: Match strength 0..1 (0 = identity/no-op, 0.5 = halfway, 1.0 = full match). Default 1.0

verbs.result: {clip, reference, space:"rgb", strength, identity, derived:{contrast, brightness, saturation, gamma, temperature_k?}, stats:{target:{mean_r,mean_g,mean_b,std_r,std_g,std_b,mean_luma,std_luma,mean_chroma,std_chroma}, reference:{…}}, sampled_at_s:{target, reference}, analysis_note, op_ids} — the derived grade is COMMITTED as an edit.grade op (op_ids); undo/history track that op. analysis_note states the v1 limits: single representative mid-clip frame, RGB sampling, gamma identity, no green-magenta tint model

verbs.name: edit.auto_balance
verbs.description: ONE-CLICK REFERENCE-FREE auto white-balance + exposure on a media clip — a standard 'Auto Color' / 'Balance Color' workflow. Unlike edit.color_match it needs NO reference clip: it samples ONE representative mid-clip frame of clip, NEUTRALISES the frame's OWN colour cast and NUDGES exposure toward a mid-luma target, then DERIVES an edit.grade correction — brightness from the luma-mean delta toward the mid target, contrast a gentle deadbanded pull of the luma spread toward a sane value, temperature_k from the warm/cool (R-B) cast pushed toward neutral (a warm cast cools, a cool cast warms) — scaled by strength (0 = identity/no-op, 1.0 = full correction, default 1.0). mode 'gray_world' (default) assumes the WHOLE-frame average should be neutral grey; mode 'white_patch' measures the cast from the bright NEAR-NEUTRAL region (the highlights that 'should be' white) — more robust when a big saturated object would skew the gray-world average (falls back to gray-world when no such highlights exist). The correction is APPLIED through the normal edit.grade path, so it composes / undoes / replays like any per-clip grade (it OVERWRITES any existing grade). The colour ANALYSIS is live (decodes one frame); the COMMITTED op is a plain, replay-safe grade (concrete params, no resampling on replay). An already-neutral, well-exposed frame derives a near-identity grade (a clean no-op), NOT an error. v1 LIMITATIONS: single mid-clip frame; plain RGB (LAB is the perceptual fast-follow); saturation is left untouched (no principled reference-free target); edit.grade has no green-magenta tint knob, so only the warm/cool axis of the cast is corrected. Video media clips only.

clip.description: Target clip id (a media clip on a video track) — the shot to balance

strength.description: Correction strength 0..1 (0 = identity/no-op, 0.5 = halfway, 1.0 = full correction). Default 1.0

mode.description: White-balance method: 'gray_world' (default — the whole-frame average should be neutral grey) or 'white_patch' (the bright near-neutral highlights should be white; robust to a big colour object)

verbs.result: {clip, mode, strength, identity, derived:{contrast, brightness, saturation, gamma, temperature_k?}, stats:{mean_rgb:[r,g,b], mean_luma, channel:{mean_r,…,std_luma,mean_chroma,…}, highlight_warmth?}, sampled_at_s, analysis_note, op_ids} — the derived grade is COMMITTED as an edit.grade op (op_ids); undo/history track that op. highlight_warmth is the bright near-neutral region's warmth used by white_patch (null for gray_world or when no highlights qualified). analysis_note states the v1 limits: single representative mid-clip frame, RGB sampling, saturation/gamma identity, no green-magenta tint model

verbs.name: edit.matte
verbs.description: AI BACKGROUND REMOVAL/REPLACE on a media clip — a straight-alpha subject cutout WITHOUT a green screen for talking-head workflows. Stores a per-clip MATTE intent; the alpha is baked by the matting sidecar (RVM by default — portable, automatic, license-clean as a user-side runtime) and cached content-addressed by the source. mode 'remove' (default) DROPS the background to reveal the track BELOW — OVERLAY clips ONLY (refused on the base track: nothing under the canvas to reveal; put the subject on a video track ABOVE the background). mode 'replace' fills behind the subject with bg (a solid colour or an asset) and is allowed on any video clip. model 'rvm' (default) | 'matanyone' (opt-in, NVIDIA + non-commercial, user-fetched). quality 'good' (default, native edges) | 'fast' (coarser, quicker). enabled:false CLEARS the matte. Matte routes the timeline to the SOFTWARE renderer (baked-alpha alphamerge composite). Media clips on video tracks only (audio/captions have no pixels).

clip.description: Clip id (a media clip on a video track; an OVERLAY track for mode=remove)

mode.description: remove = drop the background (reveal the lower track); replace = fill behind with bg. Default remove.

model.description: Matting model. Default rvm (portable, automatic, license-clean). matanyone = opt-in NVIDIA + non-commercial upgrade.

quality.description: Quality/speed tradeoff. Default good (native downsample, best edges); fast = coarser/quicker.

seed.description: PREMIUM target selection (model=matanyone only): a CLICK or box on one frame → SAM2 makes the first-frame subject mask MatAnyone2 propagates ('pick WHICH subject'). Omit for the RVM auto-seed (finds 'the human'). A different pick re-bakes.

at_ms.description: Source time (ms) of the frame the click was made on.

point.description: Positive click [x,y] in SOURCE pixels — the subject to KEEP.

bbox.description: Subject box [x,y,w,h] in SOURCE pixels (alternative to point).

bg.description: Replace-mode background (mode=replace only): a solid colour or an asset painted behind the subject.

type.description: color = solid fill; asset = an imported image/video id.

asset.description: Imported asset id painted behind the subject (type=asset).

enabled.description: false clears the matte (renders byte-identical to un-matted). Default true.

include_inverse.description: Deprecated compatibility option. Accepted for v0.6 callers but new operations use recompute-by-replay and have no inverse payload to include.

verbs.result: {op} — committed-op ride-along; the matte intent (old/new) is in op.effects[].detail. The alpha bake + the flicker/coverage receipt ride along with the render bake step.

verbs.name: edit.effect
verbs.description: SET a media clip's per-clip EFFECTS list (the 'one-click effects' pass), replacing any existing effects; an empty list clears them. Each effect maps to a CPU-only ffmpeg filter applied IN ORDER. VISUAL effects (video-track clips, after the grade stage): `vignette` {amount 0..1} darkened corners; `sharpen` {amount 0..3} unsharp mask; `blur` {radius px sigma} gaussian blur; `grain` {amount 0..100} film-grain noise; `chroma_key` {color (name or 0xRRGGBB), similarity 0..1, blend 0..1} greenscreen — keys `color` to TRANSPARENT so a LOWER track shows through (OVERLAY clips ONLY — refused on the base track: nothing under the base to reveal; put the subject on a video track ABOVE the background). `mirror` (hflip — un-mirror a webcam/selfie) · `flip` (vflip) · `hue_shift` {degrees} rotate all colors · `rgb_split` {amount px} chromatic-aberration / glitch · `pixelize` {size px} mosaic / retro · `sepia` vintage tone · `auto_color` {amount 0..1} one-click auto contrast + white balance (the 'fix dull footage' button). AUDIO effect (audio-track clips, in the audio chain): `denoise` {amount 0..1} voice/noise reduction (afftdn) — cleans hiss/hum/room tone · `compressor` {amount 0..1} dynamics compressor (acompressor) — evens out loud/quiet speech, auto makeup gain (great for talking-head/podcast). An effect must match its clip's track (visual→video, denoise→audio); an unknown `type`/bad field is a structured error (no broken filter reaches the renderer). COMPOSE ORDER (visual): crop -> conform -> grade -> EFFECTS -> overlay transform. Any effect routes the timeline to the SOFTWARE renderer (these have no CUDA filter).

clip.description: Media clip id to set effects on.

effects.description: Ordered effect list (replaces the clip's current effects; [] clears).

amount.description: vignette 0..1 / sharpen 0..3 / grain 0..100 / denoise 0..1 / compressor 0..1 / gate 0..1 / vhs 0..1 (retro-tape intensity) (audio: gate=noise gate, kills room tone between phrases)

levels.description: posterize colour levels per channel 2..64 (fewer = more banded; default 8). invert + emboss take no params.

degrees.description: hue_shift rotation in degrees (0 = none, 180 = complementary). mirror (hflip) + flip (vflip) take no params.

include_inverse.description: Deprecated compatibility option. Accepted for v0.6 callers but new operations use recompute-by-replay and have no inverse payload to include.

verbs.result: {op} — committed-op ride-along; the before/after effects list is in op.effects[].detail (old_effects, effects)
